cards.title: Artifacts in my style
cards.rule: Juan on the Osmotic Ventures identity artifact, 2026-09-03: "I love it." Then the standing preferences for every artifact "in my style" from now on:
cards.why: Why: the artifact is his operating surface for the project, not a report; it has to launch work and show exactly where he is needed. He wants them to keep getting better on their own, at scale, rather than being rewritten by hand one at a time. How to apply: default for every plan/report artifact; no need to ask. Related: [[reference_agency-visual]], [[pm-department]], [[feedback_desktop-artifact-shortcut]], [[feedback_explicit-names-not-evocative]].
cards.session_note: 2 goals + sourced facts + agency:// link sheet; OS tokens, Desktop shortcut

cards.title: Do it yourself
cards.rule: Juan, 2026-09-13, mid the iMessage bridge setup: "remember that my preference is that you do these things yourself. remember forever." Said right after he asked to "open it on my screen" and then clarified he meant the actual Settings screen he'd have to work in, not just the artifact.
cards.why: Why: he would rather I drive the mouse/keyboard through a native app's UI (via System Events, screenshots to verify state, System Events clicks with correct point-vs-pixel coordinates on Retina) than write him a numbered list and wait for him to click through it himself. A written plan is the fallback, not the first move, when the step is something an agent CAN physically do on this Mac (a Settings pane, a form, a toggle), as opposed to a true human-only wall (typing a password, entering a 2FA code that arrived on a device I can't read, an irreversible send/payment).
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: drive the app yourself; find a fix before reporting a wall

cards.title: Desktop artifact shortcut standard
cards.rule: Every published artifact gets a Desktop `.webloc` shortcut, in the same turn as the publish, unprompted. Not conditional, not a separate errand, every artifact every time; a link that only exists in terminal scrollback has not been delivered.
cards.why: Why: a plain `.webloc` with the default globe icon and a `.webloc`-suffixed name reads as a leftover technical file, not a considered shortcut on the same shelf as Juan's other app icons.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: every artifact gets a Desktop .webloc, desktop_shortcut.py

cards.title: feedback-fix-root-cause-not-a-note
cards.rule: When a record is wrong (a mis-kinded activity, a bad field, a wrong classification), the fix is to correct the record itself, not bolt an explanatory note onto it and call it done. Juan's words (2026-09-08, on a Call vs Meeting mistake in NutriBiotic HubSpot/OS): "this is the main way to fix things is to change the root cause not add a note and thats it."
cards.why: Why: a note-only fix leaves the wrong classification standing everywhere it's read (dashboards, feeds, counts) and only the reader who happens to open that specific note ever learns the truth. It also compounds: a prior attempt at this exact fix (2026-08-20) added a correction note in HubSpot but never touched the OS's own correction ledger, so the activity feed kept showing "Call" for 20 days until Juan caught it a second time.

cards.title: feedback-my-style-means-os-playbook
cards.rule: When Juan says "my style" (or similar shorthand) for a NutriBiotic deliverable, it refers to the live `/nutribiotic` OS's own design system, the one running in `portfolio/src/app/nutribiotic/lib/ui.tsx` (Card, PageHead, Ico, TierChip) and rendered at `/nutribiotic/playbook`. He said so explicitly 2026-08-13: "nutribiotic OS style (refer to playbook when I say something like this)".
cards.why: Why: Individual print pieces in `12-field-materials/` sometimes drift to their own bespoke, more muted palette for print-specific reasons (e.g. the offer sheets dialed the green back because "the color was too much" for that specific piece, per that folder's README). That per-document decision does NOT override the OS system as the default reference whenever Juan invokes "my style" without further qualification.

cards.title: No document change history
cards.rule: A document states the current best understanding, full stop. It never tells the reader how it changed across drafts: no "retire the X claim," no "the range in earlier material," no "replaces earlier pricing," no "version 2," no "previously we said," no changelog or "what's new" block. An outdated figure is replaced by the current sourced figure silently, not flagged as superseded.
cards.why: Why: Juan on the Metri Bio Marketing Guide (2026-09-13): "nothing on meta data of this document so don't record how this document has been changed over its drafts and that's something that you should remember for the whole agency is that I don't want you to tell me in the document how the document has changed. I just want you to put the most latest updated version. That is most accurate to our understanding now." The guide had a row saying to "retire the 70% to 80% claim" and a caption citing "a tertiary source that matches the range in earlier material."
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: never record draft history/"retired" meta in a deliverable

cards.title: Design/UI skill stack
cards.rule: Standing rule (Juan, 2026-06-20): for any non-trivial UI work (new UI, redesign, a dashboard, a landing page, a real component, motion, "make this look good"), reach for the design skills below before hand-rolling markup. A copy tweak or one-CSS-value fix doesn't need them.
cards.session_note: STANDING RULE: use design skills before hand-rolling any non-trivial UI

cards.title: Lead with action, bold the ask
cards.rule: Juan, 2026-08-31: "you tell me waaay to much. lead with action in your responses. What do you need me to do in Bold text." Reconfirmed 2026-09-12, after a self-caught, self-fixed script error got disclosed anyway: "never tell me the hiccups you had if you can figure them out."
cards.why: Why: he is the gate and the reader of outcomes, not an audience for process (P6). Explaining the journey to the fix competes with the fix for his attention, and a resolved hiccup carries zero decision value for him.
cards.session_note: action/outcome first line, cut narration, **bold** the ask

cards.title: Icons, not emojis
cards.rule: ABSOLUTE, agency-wide: never use emojis (🧴🌹💧✴️ etc.) anywhere in any product UI. Always use high-quality, editorial, styled icons instead, hand-drawn SVG line/silhouette glyphs in the brand ink, consistent stroke weight, crisp at any size.
cards.why: Why: emojis render inconsistently across platforms and read as cheap/unstyled; they break the luxury, editorial feel Juan wants (reference: clean line-art flacon, not the OS bottle emoji).
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: never emojis in a UI; use styled SVG icons

cards.title: feedback-call-prep-no-meta-no-sourcing
cards.rule: Call-prep artifacts (chuleta, discovery-call prep, meeting crib sheets) cut two things on sight:
cards.why: Why: Juan, on the Oscar/Plameca discovery-call prep (2026-09-15): "no quiero esto... nunca" on framework-narration, and "never say where info is from in call prep, rarely ever do i want it."

cards.title: No warning-box styling
cards.rule: Never use a rust-colored, icon-plus-tinted-background "warning sign" box to flag an open question, unconfirmed fact, or data gap in an artifact. Fold it into plain paragraph text, bold the lead phrase for emphasis if needed, no icon, no background tint, no border.
cards.why: Why: Juan, on the NutriBiotic Whale Hunting and Market Segmentation artifacts (2026-09-04): "remove these warning signs... i dont like this kind of thing in my designs." It over-uses rust, which `resources/artifacts/STANDARD.md` reserves for one real cliff/warning, diluting that signal.
cards.session_note: no rust/warning alert boxes in artifacts; fold the content into prose

cards.title: Confirm + success note
cards.rule: Any one-tap confirm control (a candidate pill, "YES!" button, "Approve" button, anything that writes real data on a single tap without a form) must be followed by a visible success note, inline, in the exact surface the tap happened on. Never silent, never a toast that can be missed.
cards.why: Why: Juan, 2026-08-19: "I've seen that success notes are important so keep this idea of buttons with success notes upon use."
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: every one-tap confirm ends in inline SuccessNote

cards.title: Short matter-of-fact titles
cards.rule: Titles and headlines (page h1, cover title, section header) are short and matter-of-fact: a product name or a plain noun phrase, never a full sentence selling the reader on why the page matters.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "the titles are way too long... this is a standing rule to make titles shorter and more matter-of-fact." A long headline reads as marketing copy narrating the page instead of naming what's on it.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: headlines are a short noun phrase, never marketing prose

cards.title: Compounding enrichment effort
cards.rule: Any Places/web enrichment lookup (not just the field it was asked to check) must write every real incidental finding, a phone, address, website, or decision-maker name, to every system that reads it as a fact: the OS table, HubSpot, and a new contact row where a person was found, in the same turn, subject to the same blank-fill-only/never-overwrite-curated rules as the narrow task. Provenance must log the real tool and query used ("google_places: category search"), not the agent's own name, and a few written rows must be spot-checked, not just trusted from the agent's own summary.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "all of this entail and searching should always be compounding effort... the tool used should be logged, and all of the findings should go into their specific locations." A prior run claimed it logged provenance but the ledger came back empty on spot-check.
cards.session_note: route every incidental finding to OS + HubSpot, not only what was asked

cards.title: First person in his own documents
cards.rule: Any document that is Juan's own operating material, not a report handed to him, speaks in his voice: "I," "my," "mine," never "Juan carries," "Juan's book," written about him from outside. This extends to UI copy inside the document too: a gate marker reads "My hand / I send it," not "Your hand / You send it."
cards.why: Why: 2026-09-04, consolidating the NutriBiotic segmentation artifacts: "speak from I not from Juan 3rd person."
cards.session_note: his own operating docs speak as I/my, never third-person "Juan"

cards.title: No explanatory UI subtext
cards.rule: In a live app screen, never add a subtext/caption explaining what the user is already looking at or how to use it ("click for drawer," "hover for why"); if a screen needs that to be understood, fix the UI's clarity instead of papering over it with prose. In artifacts/documents the same default applies (stricter than [[feedback_subtext-five-words-max]]'s length cap): no lede under a heading unless it carries a claim or insight the reader needs, never one that just describes the section or restates what a chart plots.
cards.why: Why: Juan, repeatedly (NutriBiotic Outbound, Metri Bio Six-Month Plan): "I don't really like subtexts that explain what you're looking at... just make it so obvious that you don't need text," and an explainer subtext "shows that this is AI."
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: no caption explaining a screen or how to use it, reads as AI

cards.title: Secrets and .env are never Juan's
cards.rule: Juan never handles `.env` files, secret rotation, or key management, no exceptions. The agent generates, writes, and pushes secrets end-to-end via CLI, rotates on leak immediately and silently (no asking, no warning first), and reports only that it's done, never a value. The one case that still reaches him: a credential that only exists behind an interactive login (OAuth consent, a dashboard's one-time "Copy" button). Even then, drive his Chrome to the exact button and ask for the single click, never a file edit.
cards.why: Why: this is the credential-specific instance of [[feedback_minimize-juans-manual-work]], the part of the job he finds most alien; secrets never go into chat regardless ([[feedback_never-screenshot-a-secret]]).
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: agent rotates keys + edits .env end to end, silently

cards.title: Subtext five words max
cards.rule: Every subtext under a heading (section ledes, deks, card subtitles, chart captions used as subtitles) is at most five words and never a run-on sentence. Longer ones get cut to the point or deleted.
cards.why: Why: Juan on the Metri Bio plan (2026-09-13): "no subtexts with the words run on or any subtext longer than 5 words," they "look ai." Passed examples: "Four to build by April." / "Yield against effort."
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: any lede/subtitle under a heading is at most 5 words

cards.title: feedback-new-prospect-data-to-os-immediately
cards.rule: The moment a new confirmed fact exists on a prospect (phone, address, confirmed business name), it becomes a real account row in the department's OS immediately, not just a chat reply or a route label. An unconfirmed field stays blank, noted in `quirks`, never guessed. This covers the internal OS only: creating the HubSpot company is a separate, more deliberate, human-reviewed step, not implied by this rule.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "this is the standard when we start a new client, I want their data to go to the OS account data as soon as we have anything new," so the OS stays the live record, not a report he has to transcribe from later.

cards.title: Bound every append
cards.rule: Every append needs its bound written in the same commit as the append, not later. Before committing anything that runs on a loop or cron: what does this write and what removes it, what does it read every cycle and how does it know the read was necessary, and does it ever rewrite an identical value (a no-op write still bumps `updated_at` and invalidates caches).
cards.why: Why: unbounded growth has caused three incidents (a 615MB sync-log table, a Supabase egress suspension from re-reading all accounts every cycle, an unrotated launchd log), each caught only by instrumenting and measuring, never by assuming a size "looked healthy."
cards.session_note: STANDING RULE: anything that appends gets its bound written in the same change

cards.title: No em dash
cards.rule: Never use the em dash (—, U+2014) anywhere in the agency: website copy, code comments, commit messages, chat/Telegram, memory files, docs, drafts. The en dash as a punctuation separator is out too. Use a comma, colon, period, or middot (·) for title/label separators instead.
cards.why: Why: Juan finds the em dash an obvious "AI wrote this" tell and dislikes it.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: never an em dash anywhere; style_check.py refuses the publish

cards.title: Explicit names, not evocative
cards.rule: Every name Juan sees (artifact title, Desktop shortcut, PDF, report, doc heading) says what the thing plainly IS, not a metaphor drawn from it, so he knows what he's looking at without opening it or remembering the conversation that produced it. Explicit does not mean long: two to four words naming the subject itself, not an appended "Name: what it is" explainer either.
cards.why: Why: Juan, renaming a migration runbook titled *The Fault Line*: "the fault line is epic naming but not conducing to anything tangible. make sure i immediately understand." Renamed *Claude Agency Migration*.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: name a deliverable for what it IS, not an evocative title

cards.title: No unknown-language
cards.rule: A field with no data renders as absent (omit the row/section), never as placeholder text like "unknown" or "not known yet." A true zero/count states the plain fact ("$0," "No activity logged"), that's not epistemic hedging. Exception: action-prompt chips like "No site on file" / "No phone on file" (`ReachLinks`) are a deliberate different pattern telling the rep what to go find, not banned by this rule.
cards.why: Why: Juan: placeholder prose reads as the app narrating its own ignorance back at the rep mid-field, noise at the exact moment they need signal.
cards.session_note: a missing field renders absent, never "unknown"/placeholder prose

cards.title: No monospace eyebrows
cards.rule: Never use a monospace font anywhere, in any artifact, document, or website, internal or external, no exception for data, timestamps, code, or a client site. Separately, use eyebrow/kicker labels sparingly, only where a label genuinely earns a real section break, not as decoration on every subheading, tag, or table header; when one is warranted, set it in the page's title serif (italic) or the body sans, never mono.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "I don't like that eyebrow design, looks very computer generated... zeros and ones," then confirmed "no monospace eyebrow ever please," flat, no exception, no need to ask.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: monospace forbidden agency-wide; eyebrow/kicker labels sparingly

cards.title: Never say ship
cards.rule: Never use "ship", "shipping", "ships", or "shipped" in any deliverable, deck, doc, post, or message. Use "out", "live", "published", "delivered", "goes out" instead.
cards.why: Why: Juan (2026-08-27, on a Metri Bio marketing deck): "don't use the word ship, this is not coding... this reads like AI." It's software jargon leaking into non-software work, one of the clearest AI tells.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: never the word ship/shipping/ships in anything Juan produces

cards.title: no-spark-icon
cards.rule: Never use the spark icon, or any sparkle/star-burst shape, anywhere in the agency UI.
cards.why: Why: Juan has rejected it repeatedly; it's permanently banned.

cards.title: no-signin-guard
cards.rule: Never add `alert("Sign in to ...")` or any blocking sign-in guard on an action only reachable once already logged in. If Supabase may be unconfigured, guard silently on `if(!SB) return;`, never on `SB_ON`; an auth error surfaces inline from the write call itself, no pre-flight alert needed.
cards.why: Why: the guard is logically impossible (visible button means already signed in) and has alerted Juan while already authenticated, repeatedly.

cards.title: Page numbers only over 3 pages
cards.rule: Only print a page number (e.g. "01 / 2") in a document's header or footer when it has more than three pages. A 1-3 page piece carries no page-number chrome at all.
cards.why: Why: Juan (2026-09-04), agency-wide: on a short document the count is dead weight, not orientation a reader needs.
cards.session_note: agency-wide: no page-number chrome on a 1-3 page document

cards.title: Never abbreviate wholesale
cards.rule: Never print "whsl." in any NutriBiotic field-materials document, including tight table column headers; always spell out "Wholesale"/"wholesale" in full, widen the column instead of abbreviating.
cards.why: Why: Juan rejected the "tight table layout" exception explicitly, the rule is absolute.
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: no "whsl.", widen the column instead

cards.title: CV format
cards.rule: HARD: no tagline/headline between contact info and summary; summary is exactly 3-4 rendered lines; the CV is always exactly one page, verified by rendering the deployed PDF and counting pages, never guessed; every skill category, including Languages, gets its own bullet.
cards.session_note: no tagline; summary 3-4 lines; always one page; every skill category gets bullets

cards.title: Collateral content rules
cards.rule: Never print "X% five star" next to an Amazon star rating in any NutriBiotic sales collateral; show the star rating (e.g. "4.7 out of 5") and review count only.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "the % of five-star is not needed. its a shitty metric, never use it."
cards.session_note: ABSOLUTE: no "% five star", no "no questions asked"; read reviews before quoting

cards.title: No "no questions asked"
cards.rule: Never use the phrase "no questions asked" anywhere in NutriBiotic sales collateral, even next to the 60-day money-back guarantee; state the guarantee as the plain fact instead ("Money back within 60 days of purchase").
cards.session_note: never print that phrase in NutriBiotic collateral, guarantee or not

cards.title: eisenhower-todos-safety
cards.rule: ABSOLUTE: never strip or overwrite content between `<!--TODOS:START-->` and `<!--TODOS:END-->` in any overview HTML file; run `python3 scripts/sync_graph.py` immediately after any write to one.

cards.title: commit-push-same-turn-always
cards.rule: Commit and push in the same turn as any verified edit, unasked, across every repo and submodule, not only when explicitly requested that turn.
cards.why: Why: Juan: "always in one turn," after an edit sat uncommitted until asked separately.
